sermon.title: Adding Knowledge
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this short fifth session on Bible morality, the speaker teaches that knowledge must be added to faith and virtue, and lists the five rewards of 2 Peter 1. He gives the marks of someone with Bible knowledge, cites Hosea 4:6 and Romans 6:23, and recounts Bible examples of sin’s consequences and God’s dealings with nations. He closes with calls to respond to Jesus, to defend religious freedom, and to separate spiritual harm from criminal harm.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The recording does not state the speaker’s name; the “Bible morality” theme matches Pastor Kincer’s other messages, but his name is not spoken, so Michael should confirm. This is the fifth session (“in this fifth session”) of “Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors.” Reference notes: “1935 of Genesis” is Genesis 19:35; “Second Samuel 13 2” is the account in 2 Samuel 13 and the captions garbled the name of David’s son (marked [unclear]); he cites “Second Chronicles 21 9” where the king’s killing of his brothers is in 2 Chronicles 21:4 and the disease of the bowels in 21:18–19; “Herod Agrippa” (Acts 12:21–23) and “hosea 4 verse 6” are as spoken. Caption words “Foreign” (at the start and end) were removed, and “payment,” “warred,” “wild beasts,” “abridging,” “Joram” are caption corrections; one word before “brimstone” is [unclear]. This message is highly political and sensitive: it covers homosexuality and other sexual conduct, the First Amendment, secular humanism and atheism, the Supreme Court and Congress, the United Nations and NATO, and “civil rights.” These are his own views and are not endorsed or verified here.

Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. “If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they empty it, and make it so desolate that no man may pass through because of the beasts, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; only they would be delivered, and the land would be desolate. “Or if I bring a sword on that land, and say, ‘Sword, go through the land,’ and I cut off man and beast from it, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but only they themselves would be delivered. “Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out My fury on it in blood, and cut off from it man and beast, even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness.”

faqs.question: Which empires does he say God named?
faqs.answer: He says God named “Assyria Babylon Persian and Greek empires that would deal with Israel,” and that Jesus came in “the next empire after the grecian empire rome.”

faqs.question: What does he say will bring God’s blessing on nations?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s Bible morality that’s going to cause God to bless the nations,” and that the United Nations and NATO “cannot prevent these things from happening unless they start promoting Bible morality and not weapons.”

faqs.question: What choice does he put before listeners?
faqs.answer: He says “we must choose if we are going to be a wimp or a warrior fighting against anti-bible morality bullies,” and to “respond to Jesus above our opinions.”

faqs.question: How does he separate spiritual harm from criminal harm?
faqs.answer: He says “spiritual harm is dealt with by teaching spiritual truths,” but “criminal harm immoral harm is dealt with by the punishment of the criminal,” and “crime is not to be authorized and legislated by our civil government.”
